summary: On 26 May 2020 Indonesia's Permanent Mission to the UN sent a note verbale to Secretary-General António Guterres, in the exchange triggered by Malaysia's December 2019 CLCS submission, stating that China's nine-dash line map and claim of historic rights lacked any basis in international law, invoking the 12 July 2016 arbitral award, and affirming that Indonesia has no territorial dispute with China.
actors: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Indonesia to the United Nations; Ministry of Foreign Affairs
reasoning: A circular note to the UN contesting China's claim is a formal verbal assertion of Indonesia's legal position; declarative. The note itself is a scanned UN PDF that could not be checked, so press/analysis sources are cited.

location_name: South China Sea / North Natuna Sea
summary: On 12 June 2020 Indonesia sent a second note to the UN Secretary-General replying to China's 2 June letter, which had proposed negotiating 'overlapping claims': Indonesia stated that under UNCLOS 1982 there were no overlapping claims with China and that it saw no legal reasoning under international law to negotiate maritime boundaries with China; Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi said there was no reason to negotiate.
actors: Permanent Mission of the Republic of Indonesia to the United Nations; Foreign Minister Retno Marsudi
reasoning: A UN note rejecting China's offer of boundary talks and denying any overlap is a verbal assertion of Indonesia's EEZ position; declarative. The original is a scanned UN PDF not checked by the importer.

location_name: Java Sea and South China Sea (Singkep, Riau Islands)
summary: From 18 to 26 July 2020 the Indonesian Navy's Fleet Command I held its most complex exercise of the year in the Java Sea and the South China Sea, with 2,000 personnel, 26 warships, 19 aircraft and 18 marine combat vehicles, including an amphibious landing at Singkep in the Riau Islands, staged amid the Natuna tensions and described by officials as designed to be like real operations.
actors: Indonesian Navy (TNI AL), Naval Fleet Command I (Rear Adm. Ahmadi Heri Purwono)
reasoning: A large naval exercise in waters adjoining the contested area is a show of force without confrontation; demonstrative. Low confidence because the exercise area (Singkep, Java Sea) lies well south of the Natuna EEZ that China contests.

location_name: North Natuna Sea off Natuna Regency, Riau Islands
summary: On Sunday 26 July 2020 the Bakamla patrol boat KN Pulau Dana-323 chased a Vietnamese-flagged fishing boat suspected of illegal fishing in the North Natuna Sea, which discarded its net, burned tyres to obscure visibility and attempted to ram the patrol boat; after a warning shot the patrol boat fired on the vessel until it slowed and was captured with about two tons of fish aboard (one of several Vietnamese boats seized in the North Natuna Sea that year).
actors: Maritime Security Agency (Bakamla), KN Pulau Dana-323 (Lt. Col. Hananto Widhi)
reasoning: Firing on and seizing a Vietnamese fishing boat in the overlapping EEZ area is physical interference imposing punishment; coercive. Recorded as the year's representative instance of continuing arrests of Vietnamese boats.

sources.title: Bakamla nabs Vietnamese fishing boat crew after cat-and-mouse game in Natuna
sources.excerpt: the foreign vessel had been detected on Sunday by Indonesian patrol boat KN Pulau Dana-323

summary: From the night of 11 September 2020 Bakamla tracked China Coast Guard ship 5204 inside Indonesia's EEZ in the North Natuna Sea; on 12 September the patrol ship KN Nipah 321 closed to within a kilometre, and the two ships exchanged radio messages each affirming its nation's claim to the area, Bakamla shadowing the vessel until it left the North Natuna Sea at 11:20 on Monday 14 September after almost three days.
actors: Maritime Security Agency (Bakamla), KN Nipah 321
reasoning: Intercepting, warning and shadowing a Chinese government vessel until it left the EEZ is physical interference and a warning directed at another claimant's vessel; coercive (a coder may see it as demonstrative since no force was used).

actors: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (spokesman Teuku Faizasyah)
